title: tenant-aware change detector with encrypted shadow evals
creator: Lena Morales
description:
Problem: Model/config changes and rollout actions can cause regressions in tenant-facing outputs. For Dedicated and Private customers we must provide per-tenant, privacy-preserving eval checks that run automatically on relevant config/model changes and gate rollouts when a meaningful regression is detected.

Solution overview: Build a tenant-aware change detector that executes encrypted shadow evals in a tenant-local context (sidecar for Private, isolated runner for Dedicated). The runner compares post-change outputs against tenant-specific golden evaluations (customer-provided or synthetically derived) but only transmits non-reversible telemetry (hashes, differential metrics, and cryptographic attestations) to Redwood. The service plugs into rollout orchestration so canary and full rollouts are halted or flagged if regression thresholds are exceeded.

This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria and rollout gating rules; engineering tickets will follow for sidecar implementation, metrics hashing, rollout integration and console surface.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant eval harness can be scheduled on model/config change events for Private and Dedicated deployments
Eval runner collects a configurable tenant golden set and synthetic probes; outputs are locally compared to avoid raw content exfiltration
Only hashed output deltas and aggregate metrics are emitted to Redwood control plane; no plaintext customer data leaves tenant boundary
Rollout orchestration observes the emitted metrics and prevents promotion when regression > configured threshold (default: 2% relative degradation on primary quality metric)
Tenant-level audit logs and signed attestations are stored for compliance and customer review
Console shows tenant-scoped regression report and an easy accept/rollback button for operators
success_metrics: Pilot tenants (n=3) report 0 false-blocking rollouts after two weeks of usage
Regression gating reduces post-release severity incidents by >=40% for tenants in pilot
End-to-end eval execution latency < 90s for 95th percentile of probe suites
No PII data exfiltration incidents in pilot; security review clearance granted
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize PRD and threat model; security sign-off on hashing/attestation design
Week 2: Implement sidecar runner prototype and local comparator; unit tests and smoke testing
Week 3: Integrate with rollout orchestrator (canary hook) and add console visualization
Week 4: Onboard 1 internal tenant and 2 pilot customers (opt-in); monitor, iterate thresholds
Post-pilot: Expand to Dedicated fleet and add config-based policies for automated rollback/notification
risks: Synthetic probes may not capture tenant-specific edge cases leading to missed regressions
Hashing scheme needs to balance privacy and debuggability; overly aggressive hashing makes triage hard
Resource cost of per-tenant evals could be high at scale without sensible sampling/batching
Integration complexity with Private sidecars and air-gapped deployments may delay rollout
